subject: Post-call: evaluation checklist + proposed test owners (Redwood vs cloud APIs)
messages:
From: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.com>
To: Alice Sutherland <alice.sutherland@nimbushealth.com>
Cc: Rishi Malhotra <rishi.malhotra@redwood.com>, Vivek Kulkarni <vivek.kulkarni@redwood.com>

Subject: Post-call: evaluation checklist + proposed test owners (Redwood vs cloud APIs)

Hi Alice / Ben —

Thanks again for the call today — good discussion and really appreciated the level of detail on expected traffic patterns and PII handling. Quick recap and proposed next steps so we keep momentum: 

Summary of discovery:
- Primary goal: pilot inference for clinical note summarization with strict PHI controls and end-to-end logging for audit.
- Peak concurrency target: ~120 concurrent requests during batch windows; typical 95th latency target <= 300ms per short prompt.
- Data residency requirement: US-only for this initial pilot; likely will expand to additional regions next year.

Competitive context you raised:
- You’ll be running a short evaluation vs your existing hyperscaler endpoints (G-API and A-Serve) and one boutique inference provider. Key questions: end-to-end latency, token costs, and ability to run in VPC/on-prem for compliance.

Proposed evaluation checklist (we can iterate):
1) Latency: P95 and P99 for a 512-token end-to-end request including auth/ingress.
2) Throughput: sustained 5-minute QPS ramp to emulate batch window.
3) Cost: per-token unit estimate normalized to your observed token mix.
4) Failure modes: graceful fallbacks, cold-start behavior, and cache warmup time.
5) Security: KMS integration, audit logs, and network topology validation.
6) Output quality sanity: 200 sample prompts (we can reuse your annotation set).

Suggested owners and timeline (rough):
- Redwood test harness & metrics: Vivek (setup by 12/03).
- Quality evaluation / prompt set: Marissa + Nimbus SMEs (deliverable 12/02).
- Cost normalization and reporting: Rishi (initial report 12/04).
- Final side-by-side report: target 12/08.

I attached a one-page MAAP with milestones and an initial test-specs CSV we can use as the canonical checklist. Can we confirm:
- Your infra contact for granting access to test data (SFTP or signed URLs)?
- Any additional legal/compliance gating before we spin up Dedicated or Private test endpoints?

Next meeting proposal: 30-min sync on Friday 12/03 10a PT to confirm owners and begin provisioning. If that works, I’ll send the invite and attach the access checklist.

Thanks — looking forward to running this with you.

—
Marissa Cole
Account Executive | Redwood Inference
marissa.cole@redwood.com
+1 (415) 555-0142

Attachments: 20261201-nimbus-maap.xlsx (spreadsheet), redwood-test-specs-v1.csv (csv)

Marissa — thanks for the clear recap. Helpful. A few clarifications from our side: 

- We can provide the 200 prompts and gold labels by EOD Thursday (12/02).
- For access to test data, we prefer SFTP with short-lived credentials; I’ll loop in our infra lead if needed.
- On legal gating: we need SOC2 Type II evidence and a quick read on your KMS flow before we give any live data into the pipeline. A redacted compliance pack is fine for now.

On evaluation criteria, the latency numbers look right. One additional ask: can you include a metric for token-based cost sensitivity (what happens if average token count grows by 25%)? That will help us model monthly spend.

12/03 10a PT works for a short sync. Thanks — Alice

Thanks team — I’ll own the cost-normalization and report. Quick notes on how we plan to make the comparison apples-to-apples: 

- We’ll run the same prompt set against each endpoint under identical concurrency profiles using a controlled harness.
- Cost normalization: tokenized cost per 1M tokens + amortized infra delta (e.g., Dedicated pool vs on-demand). I’ll provide a template spreadsheet for you by EOD 12/04.
- Success criteria proposal (quick):
  * Latency: P95 <= 350ms for production config (512 tokens).
  * Quality: >=85% parity on your labeling rubric for summaries.
  * Operational: ability to run in a VPC with KMS + audit logs without manual dev support.

Vivek — for the harness we discussed, can you confirm you can stand up Redwood endpoints in a dedicated test pool and produce the Prometheus/Opentelemetry metrics (p95/p99/CPU/GPU utilization) by 12/03? Also will attach the test-specs CSV to the thread for visibility.

- Rishi
